newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends U.S. holiday quietly, focus in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends U.S. holiday quietly, focus in Europe.

text.p: Traders found little reason to move the dollar during a holiday-shortened Monday session, but single-currency stirrings in Europe continued to propel sterling, which hit a new 11-month high against the dollar.
Sterling remains the safe haven currency as European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) looks more and more likely each day, traders noted.

"The pound has a psychological advantage, with a strong (U.K.) economy and the potential benefit of remaining outside EMU," said a trader at a German bank. "People are rushing to buy sterling the way they once rushed to buy Swiss francs."
U.S. trading is expected to wind down near 1300 EDT/1700 GMT, with many dealers taking the day off in observance of the Columbus Day holiday, which closed banks and the bond market.
Sterling at noon EDT/1600 GMT stood at $1.5804/09, up from $1.5778/83 at the open and $1.5748/53 at Friday's close. Sterling briefly touched an 11-month high at $1.5825 during early morning trade.
The dollar barely budged against other currencies, edging lower to 1.5280/90 marks from 1.5302/07 at the open. Against the yen, the dollar slipped to 111.60/65 from 111.64/69.
EMU got another boost Monday on news the the Finnish mark would reenter the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) with a central rate of 3.04 per mark.
ERM participation for two years is considered by many a technical requirement for joining EMU.
Italian officials have also announced their intention to reintroduce the lira to the ERM and Sweden is expected to link its currency to the group as well.
Elsewhere, the New Zealand dollar pushed briefly toward an eight-and-a-half-year high posted last month after no clear winner emerged from general elections Sunday.
The Kiwi neared the $0.7025 high from September 18, its highest point since May 1988.

"There was a lot of short-covering when we went through $0.6960 and a lot of people were stopping out there," said a dealer at an Australian bank. "But there seem to be a lot of sellers above $0.7020."
In other trade, the dollar at 1200 EDT/1600 dipped to 1.2525/35 Swiss francs from 1.2534/44 at the open. The greenback edged higher to Canadian $1.3522/27 from C$1.3520/25.
